question.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $0.05$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=4$ | $0.2$ | $0.05$ |
| $X=6$ | $0.3$ | $0.15$ |

Compute $P(X=2\,|\,Y=3)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above. Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
By the multiplication law for conditional probability, the required conditional probability is given by

$$
P(X=2\,|\,Y=3)=\frac{P(X=2,Y=3)}{P(Y=3)}=\frac{f(2,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)},
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus,

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(3) & =f(2,3)+f(4,3)+f(6,3) \\  & =0.25+0.05+0.15 \\  & =0.45.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, we have that $f(2,3)=0.25.$ 

Finally, substituting ${f}_{Y}(3)=0.45$ and $f(2,3)=0.25$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=2\,|\,Y=3) & =\frac{f(2,3)}{{f}_{Y}(3)} \\  & =\frac{0.25}{0.45} \\  & ≈0.56.\end{aligned}
$$
